# MIS 4173 Team Contract

### Team Contract
Semester: Fall 2026
Course: MIS 4173 – Systems Analysis, Design, and Development
Professor: John Drake

## Team Roles and Responsibilities

#### Facilitator: Bara

Create team agenda, keep discussions on topic, ensure every team member has an opportunity to contribute, guide the discussion when disagreements occur, monitor progress, identify issues, help coordinate responsibilities.

#### Scribe: Kyle

Record meeting notes, document action items, maintain documentation, record decisions that affect project, maintain records of feedback, and ensure notes are available to the entire team.

#### Scheduler: Ehsanullah

Scheduling meetings, coordinating times, maintaining awareness of deadlines, sending reminders, and ensuring the team has time to review before submission.

#### Role Rotation

Roles will rotate at each sprint, unless agreed upon otherwise and will be documented in the team’s project records.

## Sprint Deliverable Accountability

For every major deliverable, one team member will be designated as the accountable owner, even when other team members contribute to the work. This person is responsible for coordinating completion, making sure the deliverable meets the course rubric, ensuring deliverable is reviewed, and making sure the final version is submitted before the deadline.

| Sprint | Major Deliverable(s) | Accountable Team Member |
|---|---|---|
| Sprint 1 – Planning | Systems Request / Project Planning / Feasibility | Kyle Robertson |
| Sprint 2 – Analysis | Requirements / Use Cases / Logical Models | Bara Abusamhan |
| Sprint 3 – Analysis/Design | Analysis Refinement / Design Models | Ehsanullah Pardisi |
| Sprint 4 – Design/Implementation | Interface / Physical Models / Working System | Kyle Robertson |
| Sprint 5 – Implementation | Deployment / Security / Training / Working System | Bara Abusamhan |
| Sprint 6 – Final | Client Pitch / Final Deliverables | Kyle Robertson |

The team may change this schedule as project requirements evolve. Any changes will be documented and agreed upon by the team.

#### Individual Task Assignment

Individual tasks within each sprint will be assigned during sprint planning and documented. Each task should have an owner assigned and an expected completion date.

## Communication Norms

#### Primary Communication Tools

Our primary communication tools will be:

- Microsoft Teams: Primary channel for team communication, meetings, and project coordination.

- Email: Used for formal communication, client communication, and situations requiring a documented message.

- Shared project repository/storage: Used to maintain the current versions of project documents and other shared materials.

The team will avoid relying on private conversations between individual members for decisions that affect the entire project. Important project decisions should be communicated to the full team and documented.

#### Expected Response Times

Team members agree to respond to team communications within 24 hours on weekdays. Messages sent during evenings, weekends, holidays, or other times when a team member is unavailable may receive a response the following business day. Urgent project issues should be clearly identified as urgent rather than assuming every message requires an immediate response.

#### Meetings

The team will have a weekly stand-up meeting, with additional meetings scheduled for sprint planning, deliverable reviews, client meetings, and sprint retrospectives as needed. Meetings should begin and end on time. Members are expected to arrive prepared and participate actively. If a member cannot attend a scheduled meeting, they should notify the team at least 12 hours in advance and will review the notes afterward.

## Work Expectations and Quality Standards

### Preparation

Each team member should complete their assigned work before meetings, review the assignment requirements, and understand what the team is currently working on. If someone is confused or expects a delay, they should tell the team as soon as possible.

### Participation

Everyone is expected to attend meetings, complete their work, participate in discussions and decisions, give feedback, and help the team solve problems when needed.

### Professionalism

Team members should respect each other, communicate honestly, and take responsibility for their work. Feedback should be helpful and respectful, even when members disagree.

### Internal Review

Before submitting a major assignment, at least one other team member should review it. The review should make sure the work is accurate, complete, follows the assignment requirements, and is easy to understand.

### Acceptable Quality

Work is ready to submit when all required parts are completed, the information is accurate, and any diagrams or supporting materials are included. At least one other team member should review it, major errors should be fixed, and any AI use should be documented if required.

## Decision-Making Process

#### Consensus

The team will use consensus for major project decisions. Every member will have an opportunity to contribute ideas, ask questions, and express concerns.

#### Role-Based Authority

Routine decisions may be made by the team member who is accountable for the affected deliverable, provided the team member follows the rubric, client requirements, and agreed project goals.

#### Majority Vote

If consensus is not reached, the team will use majority votes. Before voting, members will review the available information, project requirements, constraints, and effects of every option. The facilitator will ensure that all viewpoints are considered, and the scribe will state the final decision and its rationale.

#### Resolving Dreadlocks

If a vote results in a tie, the accountable deliverable owner will recommend an option after considering the arguments. If the decision could significantly affect project scope, quality, or course compliance, the team will consult Professor Drake, GA Ashley Stocks, or the project stakeholder.

#### Final Decision

After a decision is made, all members will support it unless new information gives a reason to reconsider the decision.

## Conflict Resolution and Accountability

Disagreements and performance problems may occur during the project. Problems should be addressed early on to avoid negatively affecting the whole project.

#### 1. Direct Communication

The team member experiencing a problem should first communicate directly with the person involved in a respectful and specific manner. For example, concerns should focus on the behavior or missed expectations rather than making personal accusations.

#### 2. Team Discussion

If the issue cannot be resolved between the individuals involved, the issue will be brought to the team. The team will discuss what happened, which expectation was not met, what impact the problem had on the project, what action is needed, and how the issue can be prevented in the future.

#### 3. Corrective Action

Depending on the severity of the situation, corrective actions may include reassigning a task, adjusting a deadline, or increasing the frequency of check-ins.

#### 4. Escalation

If a significant problem continues despite reasonable attempts to resolve it internally, the team may escalate the issue to Professor Drake or GA Ashley Stocks which may result in removal from the group.

These instances include repeatedly missing meetings, not completing assigned work, submitting incomplete work, not participating, disrespectful or disruptive behavior, or any other actions that significantly jeopardize the project.

## Use of AI and Other Tools

#### Appropriate Use

Our team may use AI for brainstorming, explaining difficult concepts, creating outlines, organizing information, editing, and improving drafts, developing or reviewing code, and identifying potential issues or alternatives. AI will support but not replace our team's learning, analysis, judgment, or collaboration.

#### Review and Verification

Members must verify factual claims given by AI. Testing the code locally or using tools like Jupyter Notebook may be necessary to revise AI outputs and ensure that the content meets the rubric and client requirements.

#### Individual and Team Responsibility

All team members are responsible for verifying claims given by AI, checking code before implementation, protecting confidential client information (including API keys and proprietary information), and ensuring that the work that is submitted is understood by the entire team.

#### AI Transparency and Disclosure

Major AI use must be disclosed to the team and recorded in the AI Usage Appendix. This will identify the tool and date, purpose, prompts, summary of the output, and how the content was revised and verified. Minor spelling or grammar assistance do not require detailed disclosure.

## Contract Revision Process

This contract may be revised throughout the semester. This will serve as a living document that will allow us to solidify our work process and improve efficiency as a team. As team needs or project requirements or if existing expectations prove to be ineffective or need clarification, we may propose a revision.

The proposed revision must be discussed by the entire team before it becomes effective.

All revisions must be discussed and approved by all team members and resigned with the date to acknowledge the changes.

Previous versions of the contract will be retained so that the team has a record of how its working agreements evolved during the semester.
